title: Build a New Search Provider
readerIntent: Implement another search engine without changing provider-neutral callers.
priorKnowledge: Understand Nodics layering, provider modules, search models, pipelines, configuration, and tests.
owner: New provider module with gFramework/nSearch contract
summary: A new engine is an adapter module that registers configured connection, schema, indexing, query, lifecycle, diagnostics, and error behavior behind the shared search contract.

sections.heading: Partner handoff
items: Document supported operations, configuration, secret references, mappings, limits, unsupported behavior, local setup, production qualification, monitoring, backup, recovery, upgrade, and removal.
Register through nSearch and keep provider SDK types inside the adapter. Existing business schemas, search models, import/export, and callers must remain unchanged.
Prove that disabling the adapter restores the previous configured provider path without orphaned authority or a parallel loader.

sections.heading: Required module responsibilities
items: Declare module metadata, ownership, dependencies, configuration, documentation, AI contracts, and focused tests.
Register the engine through layered search configuration.
Own connection creation, health, readiness, close, and unique resource cleanup.
Translate provider-neutral schema and index definitions to engine mappings.
Implement normalized get, search, save, bulk, update, remove, refresh, schema, and index operations that the engine supports.
Normalize provider failures into safe SearchError behavior.

sections.heading: Configuration required
items: Engine name and activation.
Connection and schema handler service names.
Endpoint aliases and secret references.
Timeout, retry, backoff, bulk, refresh, and health policy.
Index naming, alias/version migration, tenant routing, and mapping policy.
Fallback, cacheability, diagnostics, and lifecycle options.

sections.heading: Implementation constraints
items: Do not change business callers or the generic search service for one engine.
Do not hardcode endpoints, credentials, tenants, or customer index names.
Preserve tenant/module/schema/index context.
Keep provider initialization asynchronous and outside high-volume request paths.
Keep import and export execution owned by nImport and nExport.

sections.heading: Qualification
items: Contract tests for activation, disabled behavior, every supported operation, and later-layer overrides.
Negative tests for invalid configuration, unavailable engine, mapping conflict, query failure, and partial bulk failure.
Live-provider tests for security, version compatibility, reconnect, recovery, cleanup, capacity, and tenant isolation.
Regression tests proving normal schema save/update and other providers still work.
